mainTopic: The wording and timing of the ברכה on ביעור חמץ, and the source for searching by the light of a נר
overview: The amud opens by narrowing the dispute between רב פפי and רב פפא about the ברכה on removing חמץ. Both agree that "לבער" looks to the future. They argue only about whether "על ביעור" sounds like something already done. The גמרא challenges the 'past' view from the ברכות on מילה, שחיטה and לולב, and answers each challenge by showing why that case is special. The הלכה is that one says "על ביעור חמץ". Next, the גמרא brings שמואל's rule that every ברכה is said before the מצוה (עובר לעשייתן), and proves from three פסוקים that "עובר" means 'before'. בי רב list טבילה and שופר as exceptions, but רב חסדא corrects this so that only טבילה is an exception, and a ברייתא supports him. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's rule of searching by the light of a נר. רב חסדא derives it from a chain of verses, and the school of רבי ישמעאל calls that chain a hint. Finally, a ברייתא begins to rule out sunlight, moonlight and torchlight, and its reasons continue on the next amud.

steps.title: Defining exactly where the two opinions disagree
steps.stepSummary: The dispute is only about the phrase "על ביעור". One opinion says it implies the act is already done. The other says it can refer to the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they argue is about the wording "על ביעור" (concerning the removal). One master holds it means something done earlier. The other master holds it means something still to come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pins down the exact point of the argument between רב פפי and רב פפא about the wording of the ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that "לבער" (to remove) is clearly future-looking and fits a ברכה said before the act. The only question is "על ביעור". רב פפי hears it as past tense, as if the מצוה were already finished. רב פפא says it can also mean the future, so it works before the act too.

keyTerms.meaning: it implies something from before (already done)
it implies the future (still to be done)

steps.whyThisMatters: A ברכה on a מצוה is normally said before doing it. So the question is whether "על" wording fits a ברכה said before the act. The rest of this section tests that question.

phrases.english: Where they disagree is about "concerning the removal."
phrases.notes: Both agree that "לבער" is future.

phrases.english: One master holds: it implies something done before,
phrases.notes: This is רב פפי.

phrases.english: and the other master holds: it implies the future.
phrases.notes: This is רב פפא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier dispute (on the previous amud) by narrowing exactly what it is about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is only about "על ביעור": past-sounding according to one view, future-capable according to the other.

steps.title: Challenge from the ברכה on מילה
steps.stepSummary: The ברכה on מילה uses "על המילה" and is said before the מילה. So "על" must be able to mean the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: the ברכה is "Blessed... Who made us holy with His מצוות and commanded us concerning the מילה"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the view that "על" means 'already done' by pointing to the ברכה on מילה, which is said before the מילה happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "על" only meant 'already finished', the ברכה on מילה should not use it, since it is said beforehand. The fact that it does use "על" seems to prove that "על" can refer to the future, as רב פפא says.

keyTerms.meaning: Who made us holy with His מצוות (standard ברכה wording)

phrases.english: They challenged: "Blessed... Who has made us holy
phrases.notes: The "..." stands for the standard opening words of the ברכה.

phrases.english: with His מצוות and commanded us concerning the circumcision"!
phrases.notes: This ברכה is said before the act, yet it uses "על".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'past' opinion from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that "על ביעור" means the act is already done (רב פפי).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברכה on מילה uses "על" before the act, so "על" can refer to the future.

steps.title: מילה is different: the wording "למול" would not fit
steps.stepSummary: With מילה there was no good alternative. Saying "למול" would wrongly suggest that the father himself must do the cutting.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, what else could we say? Should we say "to circumcise"? Does that mean it is not enough unless he himself circumcises?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the 'past' view: "על" was used for מילה only because there was no better option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה belongs to the father, but he may have someone else (a מוהל) do it. Saying "למול" (to circumcise) would sound as if the person saying the ברכה must cut personally. So the general wording "על המילה" was chosen. It is a special case and proves nothing about what "על" normally means.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that "על" means the future. It is saying that "על" was used here only because "למול" would give the wrong message about who must do the act.

phrases.english: There, what should we say?
phrases.notes: In other words, what other wording was possible?

phrases.english: Should we say "to circumcise"?
Is it not enough unless he himself circumcises?
phrases.notes: But the father may appoint someone else to do it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special-case explanation: the wording was forced by circumstance.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "על המילה" proves that "על" naturally means the future.
steps.terutzMaskana: "על" was used only because "למול" would wrongly suggest that the father must do the cutting himself.

steps.title: What about when the father does the מילה himself?
steps.stepSummary: If the father himself circumcises, "למול" would fit perfectly, so the earlier excuse does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: The father of the boy, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer: when the father does the מילה himself, he could say "למול".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 3 worked only when someone else does the cutting. When the father himself cuts, nothing stops him from saying "למול". So why would "על" be needed?

phrases.english: The father of the boy, what can be said?
phrases.notes: When the father is the one cutting, "למול" would be fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that "למול" could not be said.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When the father himself cuts, "למול" fits, so the excuse fails in that case.

steps.title: Yes, the father himself does say "למול"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: when the father circumcises, he does say "למול".
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the point. A father who does the מילה himself really does say "למול".
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no contradiction. "על המילה" is the wording only when someone other than the father cuts. When the father cuts, he uses the future-sounding "למול". This actually fits the view that "על" sounds like the past.

keyTerms.meaning: yes, that is indeed so (the גמרא agrees)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברכה on מילה does not prove that "על" means the future. "על" is used because a מוהל may act for the father. A father cutting his own son says "למול".

phrases.english: Yes, that is indeed so.
phrases.notes: The father who cuts says "למול".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by agreeing with it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father would also have to say "על המילה".
steps.terutzMaskana: The father says "למול". "על המילה" is said only when someone else performs the מילה.

steps.title: Challenge from the ברכה on שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: The ברכה on שחיטה uses "על השחיטה" before slaughtering, so "על" seems to mean the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: "Blessed... Who made us holy with His מצוות and commanded us concerning the slaughtering"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge of the same kind, this time from the ברכה said before שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here no father or agent is involved, so the מילה answer does not obviously help. The ברכה is said before slaughtering and still uses "על". That seems to prove again that "על" fits the future.

phrases.english: They challenged: "Blessed... Who has made us holy
with His מצוות and commanded us concerning the slaughtering"!
phrases.notes: Said before slaughtering, yet it uses "על".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge against the same 'past' view, parallel to step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that "על ביעור" means the act is already done (רב פפי).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברכה on שחיטה uses "על" before the act, so "על" can mean the future.

steps.title: שחיטה is different: "לשחוט" would sound like a duty to slaughter
steps.stepSummary: Saying "לשחוט" would wrongly suggest that a person is obligated to slaughter. So the general wording "על השחיטה" was chosen.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, what should we say? Should we say "to slaughter"? Does that mean it is not enough unless he slaughters?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the same way as with מילה: there was no good alternative to "על".
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no מצוה to go out and slaughter an animal. שחיטה is only required if you want to eat meat. Saying "לשחוט" would sound like a command to slaughter, so the ברכה uses "על השחיטה". Again, this is a special case and not proof of what "על" normally means.
steps.confusionAlert: Here "לָא סַגִּיא דְּלָאו אִיהוּ שָׁחֵט" means: is there an obligation to slaughter? It is not about who does the slaughtering, as it was with מילה.

phrases.english: There too, what should we say?
Should we say "to slaughter"?
Is it not enough unless he slaughters?
phrases.notes: No one is obligated to slaughter. It is only a step required before eating meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 using the same pattern as step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special-case explanation: the wording was forced to avoid implying an obligation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "על השחיטה" proves that "על" naturally means the future.
steps.terutzMaskana: "על" is used only because "לשחוט" would suggest a duty to slaughter, which does not exist.

steps.title: What about the קרבן פסח and other קדשים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the excuse from Step 7. With פסח and קדשים, a person really is obligated to slaughter, so ״לשחוט״ would fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: With the פסח and other קדשים, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. That answer said we avoid ״לשחוט״ because there is no obligation to slaughter, but with a קרבן פסח there is an obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7, ״על השחיטה״ was explained as a way to avoid implying an obligation to slaughter. With קרבן פסח and other קדשים, slaughtering really is required, so that excuse does not work. The question is: what ברכה is said there?

keyTerms.meaning: The Paschal offering, which a person is obligated to bring and slaughter
What can be said? (a challenge formula)

phrases.english: The Paschal offering and sacrifices
what is there to say?
phrases.notes: There, slaughtering really is an obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the excuse given in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ״לשחוט״ is avoided because there is no obligation to slaughter
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With פסח and קדשים there is an obligation, so the excuse fails in those cases

steps.title: Yes, there one says ״לשחוט״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: when slaughtering פסח or קדשים, the ברכה is ״לשחוט״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the point. For פסח and קדשים, the ברכה really is ״לשחוט״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of answer as Step 5 with מילה. Where the obligation is real, the future form ״ל...״ is used, so the general rule is not broken.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, it is indeed so (accepting the challenge)

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so.
phrases.notes: There one says ״לשחוט״.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 by agreeing with it
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession: the case is treated differently
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The excuse that ״לשחוט״ is avoided because there is no duty to slaughter seems to fail for פסח and קדשים, where there is such a duty.
steps.terutzMaskana: With פסח and קדשים one says ״לשחוט״, so the approach stays consistent

steps.title: Challenge from the blessing on לולב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that when a person picks up the לולב to fulfill the מצוה, he says ״על נטילת לולב״. This shows ״על״ is used before the מצוה is done.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: Someone who makes a לולב for himself says ״שהחיינו״. When he takes it to fulfill the מצוה, he says ״אשר קדשנו במצותיו וצונו על נטילת לולב״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as a challenge. It seems to show that ״על״ is said before doing the מצוה, so it refers to the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says he takes the לולב ״לצאת בו״, which sounds like he has not fulfilled the מצוה yet. Even so, the ברכה uses ״על נטילת״, not ״ליטול״. That goes against the idea that ״על״ means something already done.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing for a new or seasonal occasion
To fulfill the obligation with it
Concerning the taking of the לולב

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who makes a lulav for himself
blesses: "Who has given us life, sustained us,
and brought us to this time."
When he took it to fulfill the obligation with it,
he says: "Who made us holy with His commandments
and commanded us concerning taking the lulav!"
phrases.notes: ״על״ is used before the מצוה is fulfilled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source against the view that ״על״ means the past
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that ״על״ means an action already done
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא uses ״על נטילת״ before the person fulfills the מצוה (״לצאת בו״)

steps.title: Lifting the לולב already fulfills the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: With לולב, the מצוה is fulfilled as soon as he lifts it. So when he says the ברכה, the act is already done.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because once he lifted it, he already fulfilled the מצוה with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that לולב is a special case. By the moment he lifts it, the מצוה is already done, so ״על״ refers to the past after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכה is said while the לולב is already in his hand. Since the מצוה of נטילה is complete as soon as he lifts it, ״על נטילת״ describes something already done. The proof from לולב is therefore removed.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time, at the moment
He fulfilled the obligation with it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mistake this for a general rule about all ברכות. It is a specific point: with לולב, the מצוה is complete the moment it is lifted, which comes before the ברכה is finished.

phrases.english: It is different there,
for at the moment he lifted it, he fulfilled the obligation with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the לולב challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברכה on לולב comes before the מצוה, so ״על״ means the future
steps.terutzMaskana: The מצוה is done once he lifts it, so ״על״ refers to the past

steps.title: Then the ברייתא should say "he fulfilled"
steps.stepSummary: If the מצוה is already done, the ברייתא should have said ״יצא בו״ (he fulfilled with it), not ״לצאת בו״ (to fulfill with it).
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say ״לצאת בו״? It should have said ״יצא בו״!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. The ברייתא's own words, ״לצאת בו״, sound like the מצוה has not been done yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said the מצוה is already complete at the moment of lifting. If that is true, the ברייתא's wording should match it with ״יצא בו״. The challenge is about the precise wording of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: He fulfilled the obligation with it (already done)

phrases.english: If so, "to fulfill with it"?
It should have said "he fulfilled with it"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the לולב מצוה is already done when the ברכה is said
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's wording ״לצאת בו״ suggests a future act, not a past one

steps.title: Matching the wording of the סוכה clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that ״יצא בו״ would be more exact. The ברייתא said ״לצאת בו״ to match the later clause about sitting in the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. But because the ברייתא wanted to teach the later clause, ״לישב בסוכה״, it also used ״לצאת בו״ in the first clause.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits the wording is not exact for לולב. It explains that the ברייתא chose matching wording for both clauses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סוכה clause speaks of something still to come (״לישב״, to sit). To keep the two clauses parallel, the ברייתא wrote ״לצאת בו״ for לולב too. So the wording is about style and does not prove anything about the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a teaching
The first clause of a teaching

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so,
but because it wanted to teach the latter clause:
"to sit in the sukka,"
it taught in the first clause also "to fulfill with it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic parallelism: the wording follows the סיפא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״לצאת בו״ proves the לולב מצוה was not yet done
steps.terutzMaskana: ״לצאת בו״ only matches the סוכה clause and proves nothing

steps.title: Quoting the סוכה clause of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the later clause: whoever makes a סוכה says ״שהחיינו״, and when he enters to sit he says ״לישב בסוכה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the later clause teaches: Someone who makes a סוכה for himself says ״ברוך אתה ה׳ ... שהחיינו וקיימנו והגיענו לזמן הזה״. When he enters to sit in it, he says ״ברוך ... אשר קדשנו במצותיו וצונו לישב בסוכה״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the actual words of the סוכה clause. This backs up its explanation that the לולב wording was chosen to match it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סוכה clause, ״נכנס לישב בה״ really does describe a future act, and the ברכה is ״לישב״. This is the clause that the ברייתא's wording ״לצאת בו״ was made to match.

phrases.english: As it teaches in the latter clause:
One who makes a sukka for himself
says: "Blessed are You, God ...
Who has given us life, sustained us, and brought us to this time."
When he enters to sit in it,
he says: "Blessed ... Who made us holy with His commandments
and commanded us to sit in the sukka."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the clause that Step 13 relied on
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the ברייתא's רישא matches its סיפא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the ברייתא about סוכה, which uses ״לישב בסוכה״

steps.title: The final ruling: ״על ביעור חמץ״
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that the ברכה for removing חמץ is ״על ביעור חמץ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: ״על ביעור חמץ״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion with a final practical ruling. Before searching for חמץ, one says ״על ביעור חמץ״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of the proofs settled whether ״על״ means past or future. The ruling picks ״על ביעור״, a wording that can also cover a future act, so it fits a ברכה said before the ביעור.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברכה before בדיקת חמץ is ״על ביעור חמץ״. Along the way the גמרא shows: (1) ״ל...״ is used where the person himself is obligated to act (מילה by the father, פסח and קדשים); (2) with לולב, ״על נטילת״ fits because the מצוה is done as soon as he lifts it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical source for the wording of the ברכה we say every year at בדיקת חמץ.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: "concerning the removal of leaven."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the whole discussion with a final ruling
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברכה before בדיקת חמץ is ״על ביעור חמץ״, which can also refer to the future.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a ברכה comes before the מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees a ברכה must be said before the מצוה. The גמרא asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, everyone agrees that we need to say the ברכה at the start. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes something everyone agreed on in the earlier discussion: a ברכה is said before doing the מצוה. Now it asks where that rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier debate about the wording 'לבער' versus 'על ביעור', both sides assumed the ברכה is said before the act. The גמרא now wants the source for that shared assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: In any case, according to everyone,
we need to say the blessing at the start,
from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the shared assumption from the ביעור חמץ discussion and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for saying a ברכה before doing a מצוה.

steps.title: שמואל's rule: bless before doing
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: for every מצוה, the ברכה is said 'עובר לעשייתן', before the act.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: for all the מצוות, a person says the ברכה over them before he does them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a general rule from שמואל. Every מצוה gets its ברכה before it is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is a clear rule from an אמורא, not a פסוק. But the rule depends on the word 'עובר', and that word does not obviously mean 'before'. This sets up the next question.
steps.whatToRemember: The basic rule: עובר לעשייתן. The ברכה comes before the מצוה.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
for all the מצוות, one blesses over them
before ("over") their performance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל's rule: every מצוה gets its ברכה עובר לעשייתן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All מצוות get their ברכה before they are done.

steps.title: How do we know 'עובר' means 'before'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the word 'עובר' means coming first.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we see that this word 'עובר' means 'going ahead'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the key word in שמואל's rule. 'עובר' usually means 'passing', so how do we know it means 'before'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole rule depends on this one word. If 'עובר' could mean 'after' or 'while passing through', the rule would change. The גמרא wants proof from the פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: How do we see / what shows

phrases.english: From where may it be inferred that this word "over"
is the language of going first?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of the key word in שמואל's rule.

steps.title: First proof: אחימעץ overtook the Cushite
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a פסוק: אחימעץ ran and 'ויעבר' the Cushite, meaning he got ahead of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: the פסוק says, 'And אחימעץ ran by way of the plain, and passed the Cushite.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a פסוק where 'ויעבר' clearly means getting ahead of someone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two runners were bringing news to דוד. אחימעץ 'passed' the Cushite, which means he overtook him and arrived first. So the root עבר can mean 'coming before'.

keyTerms.meaning: אחימעץ, a messenger in דוד's time

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said,
for the verse says:
"And Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain,
phrases.notes: שמואל ב יח:כג

phrases.english: and overran the Cushite."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ויעבר את הכושי' means he got ahead. So עבר means 'before'.

steps.title: Second proof: יעקב went ahead of his family
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a different פסוק: 'והוא עבר לפניהם', meaning יעקב went in front of his family.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: we learn it from here: 'And he passed before them.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives another source. When יעקב went to meet עשו, he 'עבר לפניהם', meaning he walked in front of his family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק is even clearer because it adds the word 'לפניהם', 'in front of them'. It shows that עבר means going ahead of something.

keyTerms.meaning: Went ahead in front of them

phrases.english: Abaye said: from here:
"And he passed before them."
phrases.notes: בראשית לג:ג

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second source for the same point.

steps.title: Third proof: the king goes before them
steps.stepSummary: A third possible source: 'ויעבר מלכם לפניהם וה׳ בראשם', their king passes before them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say it is from here: 'And their king passed before them, and ה׳ at their head.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers one more פסוק, from מיכה, where 'ויעבר' means leading in front.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'ויעבר' is paired with 'בראשם', 'at their head'. That shows clearly that the word means being first, at the front.
steps.whatToRemember: Three פסוקים show that 'עובר' means 'before'. So the ברכה is said before the מצוה.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say it is from here:
"And their king passed before them,
phrases.notes: מיכה ב:יג

phrases.english: and God at their head."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third source for the meaning of עובר.

steps.title: בי רב: two exceptions, טבילה and שופר
steps.stepSummary: בי רב say the rule of blessing first has two exceptions: טבילה and שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רב say: except for טבילה and שופר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement limits שמואל's rule. For טבילה and שופר, the ברכה is not said before the act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule is not cancelled. It just has exceptions. The גמרא will now test whether each exception makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Immersion in a מקוה (here, of a בעל קרי)
Ram's horn blown on ראש השנה

phrases.english: In the school of Rav they say:
except for immersion and shofar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds exceptions to שמואל's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For טבילה and שופר, the ברכה is not said beforehand.

steps.title: טבילה makes sense, but why שופר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the טבילה exception, because the person cannot bless before immersing. But it asks why שופר would be an exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for טבילה, because the man is still not fit to bless. But for שופר, what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks each exception. It understands טבילה but challenges שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before immersing, the person is טמא and not fit to say a ברכה. So he blesses afterward. With שופר nothing stops the person from blessing first, so the exception seems to have no reason.
steps.confusionAlert: According to רש״י (and the translation used here), this טבילה is the immersion of a בעל קרי, who may not say a ברכה before immersing. תוספות disagree and explain it as the immersion of a גר, who cannot say 'וצונו' before he has become Jewish.

phrases.english: Granted for immersion —
since the man is still not fit (to bless).
But shofar, what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the two exceptions of step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The שופר exception in בי רב's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: טבילה has a clear reason (the person is not fit to bless yet), but שופר has no reason to be different.

steps.title: Suggested reason: the blowing might go wrong
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a reason for שופר: maybe the תקיעה will come out wrong, and the ברכה will be wasted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it is because maybe the תקיעה will be ruined —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a possible reason for the שופר exception. It will reject this reason in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea: if he blesses first and then the sound comes out invalid, he said a ברכה לבטלה. So he should bless only after a good תקיעה.

phrases.english: And if you say it is because
perhaps the blast will be ruined —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שופר exception has no reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe the reason is fear that the תקיעה fails and the ברכה is wasted.

steps.title: Rejected: then שחיטה and מילה too
steps.stepSummary: That reason fails. If so, we should also not bless before שחיטה and מילה, since those can go wrong too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even שחיטה and מילה too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggested reason. If fear of failure were enough, other מצוות would also need the ברכה afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שחיטה and מילה can also come out invalid, yet we bless before them. So 'it might go wrong' cannot explain why שופר is different.

phrases.english: If so,
then even slaughter and circumcision as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested reason of step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The 'blast might fail' reason for the שופר exception.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It proves too much. שחיטה and מילה could also fail, yet we bless before them.

steps.title: רב חסדא: only טבילה was said
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא corrects בי רב's statement. The exception was only טבילה, not שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב חסדא said: 'except for טבילה alone' is what was said.
steps.whatsHappening: Since no reason for שופר works, רב חסדא fixes the wording. The real statement listed only טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem goes away by removing שופר from the list. Now the only exception is טבילה, which has a clear reason. שופר follows the normal rule: the ברכה comes first.
steps.whatToRemember: The only exception to עובר לעשייתן here is טבילה. For שופר we bless before blowing, like all מצוות.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ḥisda said:
"except for immersion alone" was stated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge by correcting the text of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בי רב listed both טבילה and שופר as exceptions.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only טבילה was listed. שופר follows the normal rule.

steps.title: A ברייתא: bless when coming up from the טבילה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב חסדא. After immersing, as he comes up, he says the ברכה 'על הטבילה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: if he immersed and came up, as he comes up he says: 'ברוך ... אשר קדשנו במצותיו וצונו על הטבילה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רב חסדא. For טבילה, the ברכה is said after the immersion, as the person comes out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא mentions only טבילה as a case of blessing afterward. This fits רב חסדא's version. It also shows when the ברכה is said: right as he comes up from the water.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule: in this case, the ברכה for טבילה is said after immersing, as the person comes up.

phrases.english: That was also taught (in a baraita):
If he immersed and came up,
as he comes up he says:
"Blessed… Who has made us holy through His מצוות
and commanded us concerning immersion."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב חסדא's correction with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That טבילה is the exception and its ברכה is said afterward.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'טבל ועלה, בעלייתו אומר... על הטבילה'.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For טבילה, the ברכה is said as the person comes up from the water. All other מצוות get their ברכה before.

steps.title: Where does the lamp requirement come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'by the light of the lamp' and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'By the light of the lamp, etc.' From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the ברכה discussion and goes back to a new phrase in the משנה. It asks where we learn that בדיקת חמץ needs a נר. This question sets up רב חסדא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated the rule but gave no source. מנא הני מילי is a request for the scriptural basis. The גמרא wants to know why the search must use a lamp specifically, rather than daylight or some other method.

keyTerms.meaning: By the light of the lamp (a quote from the משנה)
Etc., meaning the quote continues in the משנה
From where are these words? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: [The Mishnah said:] By the light of the lamp, etc.
phrases.notes: A new quote from the משנה. This opens a new topic.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. The ברכה discussion in steps 1-27 is finished, and the גמרא returns to the wording of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for doing בדיקת חמץ by the light of a נר.

steps.title: רב חסדא's chain of word-links
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא gives a five-link chain: finding from finding, finding from searching, searching from searching, searching from lamps, and lamps from lamp.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: We learn 'finding' from 'finding,' 'finding' from 'searching,' 'searching' from 'searching,' 'searching' from 'lamps,' and 'lamps' from 'lamp.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question with a short outline of a chain of words. Each link connects one verse to the next. The גמרא will fill in the actual verses in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says חמץ must not be 'found.' רב חסדא connects 'found' to a verse where finding comes through 'searching.' He then connects searching to 'lamps' and lamps to 'lamp.' The result is that the way to make sure חמץ is not found is to search with a lamp.
steps.confusionAlert: This is only an outline. Do not try to locate the verses here. The גמרא spells them out in steps 30 and 31.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
We derive 'finding' from 'finding,'
and 'finding' from 'searching,'
and 'searching' from 'searching,'
and 'searching' from 'lamps,'
and 'lamps' from 'lamp.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לָמַדְנוּ מְצִיאָה מִמְּצִיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The lamp requirement comes from a chain of shared words: מציאה, then חיפוש, then נרות, then נר.

steps.title: The first links: from 'found' to 'searched'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the verses for the first links. 'Not be found' in the חמץ verse matches 'was found' in the story of יוסף's goblet, and in that verse the finding comes through searching.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Finding' from 'finding': it is written here, 'Seven days leaven shall not be found in your houses,' and it is written there, 'And he searched, beginning with the eldest and ending with the youngest, and it was found.' And 'finding' is connected to the 'searching' of that same verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts filling in רב חסדא's outline with real verses. It shows how the חמץ verse connects to the story of searching בנימין's sack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both verses use a form of 'found' (יִמָּצֵא / וַיִּמָּצֵא). That shared word links them. In the יוסף verse, the goblet was found only after a search, so 'finding' is tied to 'searching' within that one verse (דידיה, 'its own'). This means making sure חמץ is not found requires a search.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here (in our topic's verse)
And it is written there (in the other verse)
Its own, meaning within that same verse

phrases.english: 'Finding' from 'finding':
It is written here:
'Seven days leaven shall not be found in your houses,'
phrases.notes: שמות יב:יט

phrases.english: and it is written there:
'And he searched, beginning with the eldest,'
phrases.notes: בראשית מד:יב. This is the search for יוסף's goblet.

phrases.english: 'and ending with the youngest; and it was found.'
And 'finding' is learned from the 'searching' of that same verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first two links of רב חסדא's chain from step 29.
steps.raayaObject: The links מציאה to מציאה and מציאה to חיפוש.

steps.title: The last links: from 'search' to 'lamps' to 'lamp'
steps.stepSummary: Searching is linked to lamps through צפניה, and lamps are linked to a single lamp through משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Searching' from 'lamps,' as it is written: 'At that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps.' And 'lamps' from 'lamp,' as it is written: 'The spirit of man is the lamp of God, searching all the inward parts.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the chain. It shows that searching is done with lamps, and then that the lamps mean a single lamp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In צפניה, God 'searches' Jerusalem 'with lamps,' so a proper search uses lamps. The verse in משלי speaks of a single 'lamp' that 'searches,' which teaches that one lamp is enough. The link חיפוש מחיפוש is not spelled out here. It is the shared word 'search' that connects the יוסף verse to the צפניה verse.

keyTerms.meaning: The soul or spirit of a person
The inner chambers of the body

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא listed 'searching from searching' in step 29, but the גמרא does not give it a separate line here. The link is the word 'search' (חיפוש) appearing in both the יוסף verse and the צפניה verse.

phrases.english: And 'searching' from 'lamps,' as it is written:
'At that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps,'
phrases.notes: צפניה א:יב

phrases.english: and 'lamps' from 'lamp,' as it is written:
'The spirit of man is the lamp of the Lord,'
phrases.notes: משלי כ:כז. Some versions have the word in round brackets, but the word in square brackets is the corrected wording, the way the פסוק really reads.

phrases.english: 'searching all the inward parts.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the verse chain begun in step 30.
steps.raayaObject: The links חיפוש to נרות and נרות to נר.
steps.whyThisMatters: The final verse uses a single נר. This is why בדיקת חמץ is done with one candle rather than many lights.

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches the same rule as a hint
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from דבי רבי ישמעאל rules that on the night of the 14th we search for חמץ by lamplight. It brings the same four verses, but calls them a hint (זכר לדבר) rather than a proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: On the night of the fourteenth we search for חמץ by the light of a lamp. Although there is no proof for the matter, there is a hint to it. As it says: 'Seven days leaven shall not be found,' and it says: 'And he searched, beginning with the eldest and ending with the youngest,' and it says: 'At that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps,' and it says: 'The spirit of man is the lamp of the Lord, searching.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב חסדא's chain. It uses the same four verses in the same order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא agrees with רב חסדא on both the rule and the verses. It adds one point: these verses are only a hint (זכר לדבר), not a true proof (ראיה). The verses in בראשית, צפניה, and משלי are not about חמץ at all. So the lamp requirement is supported and hinted at by the verses, but not strictly derived from them.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל (a ברייתא)
The night of the fourteenth (of ניסן)
There is no proof for the matter
A hint or allusion to the matter

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that בדיקת חמץ is done by the light of a single נר rests on a chain of verses: found, then searched, then lamps, then lamp. The ברייתא calls this chain a hint (זכר לדבר), not an absolute proof.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא is weakening the rule. The הלכה of searching by lamplight is firm. Only the verses' status is described as a hint rather than a direct source.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
On the night of the fourteenth
we search for leaven by the light of the lamp.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לְדָבָר,
phrases.english: Although there is no proof for the matter,
there is a hint to the matter, as it is stated:
'Seven days leaven shall not be found,'
and it says: 'And he searched, beginning with the eldest and ending with the youngest,'

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמֵר: ״בָּעֵת הַהִיא אֲחַפֵּשׂ אֶת יְרוּשָׁלִַים בַּנֵּרוֹת״,
phrases.english: and it says: 'At that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps,'
and it says: 'The spirit of man is the lamp of the Lord, searching.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב חסדא's chain (steps 29-31) with a ברייתא using the same verses.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's derivation that בדיקת חמץ is done by the light of a נר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב חסדא's chain matches an older tradition. It also teaches that the verses serve as a זכר לדבר, a hint, rather than a strict proof.

steps.title: Why add the last verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed the final verse introduced with 'ואומר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason for the final 'and it says'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא added one more verse with the word 'ואומר'. The verse in צפניה already seemed to show that we search with lamps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in צפניה says God will search ירושלים 'with lamps', which already seems to prove that searching is done by lamplight. So the extra verse from משלי looks unnecessary. The גמרא wants to know what new thing it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what is the reason for
'And it says': a formula that brings an additional verse as more support

phrases.english: What is the purpose of 'and it says'?
phrases.notes: Refers to the last verse in the ברייתא: 'נר ה׳ נשמת אדם'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the structure of the ברייתא brought in step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ברייתא needed the verse from משלי after it had already quoted the verse in צפניה about searching with lamps.

steps.title: The extra verse shows that a lamp searches thoroughly
steps.stepSummary: Without the verse from משלי, one might think the verse in צפניה describes a lenient, weaker search. 'נר ה׳ נשמת אדם' shows that a lamp is the tool for a thorough search.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that this verse 'at that time' is a leniency, as the Merciful One is saying: 'I will not search ירושלים by the light of a torch, whose light is very great, but by the light of a lamp, whose light is smaller, so that a big sin will be found and a small sin will not be found.' Come and hear: 'The spirit of man is the lamp of God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the verse in צפניה alone could be read as God being lenient: searching with a dim lamp so that only big sins are found. The verse from משלי blocks that reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that a lamp was chosen because it is weaker than a torch, which would make lamp-searching a lower standard. The verse in משלי continues 'searching all the inner chambers', so a lamp is the tool of a complete, careful search. That makes it the right tool for finding every bit of חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you would say': introduces a possible wrong assumption
A torch, which gives a large, strong light
A lamp, which gives a smaller light
'The spirit of man is the lamp of God' (משלי 20:27)

steps.whatToRemember: The verse in צפניה alone might suggest a lamp is a weaker, more lenient light. The verse in משלי shows that a lamp is the tool of a thorough search.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying a lamp gives more light than a torch. A torch is brighter. The point is that a lamp is the right tool for careful searching.

phrases.english: And if you would say: this verse 'at that time'
phrases.notes: The verse in צפניה: 'At that time I will search ירושלים with lamps.'

phrases.english: is a leniency that the Merciful One is saying:
I will not search ירושלים
by the light of a torch
whose light is very great,
but by the light of a lamp
whose light is smaller,
so that a big sin will be found
and a small sin will not be found,
come and hear: 'The spirit of man is the lamp of God.'
phrases.notes: The verse continues 'searching all the inner chambers', which shows a lamp searches thoroughly.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הַאי ״בָּעֵת הָהִיא״ — קוּלָּא הוּא דְּקָאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse in צפניה could be misread as a leniency (a dim lamp so only big sins are found). The verse in משלי shows a lamp is the tool of a thorough search.

steps.title: Search only by lamplight, not by sun, moon, or torch
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that בדיקת חמץ is not done by sunlight, moonlight, or torchlight, only by the light of a lamp.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: We do not search by the light of the sun, nor by the light of the moon, nor by the light of a torch, but by the light of a lamp,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that lists which lights may not be used for בדיקת חמץ. Only a lamp is allowed, and the ברייתא is about to give the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the סוגיא proved that we search with a lamp. This ברייתא adds the negative side: other lights, even brighter ones like the sun or a torch, are not valid. The ברייתא gives the reason on the next amud.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule behind the custom of searching for חמץ with a candle and not with sunlight or a large flame.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: We do not search
not by the light of the sun,
nor by the light of the moon,
nor by the light of a torch,
but by the light of a lamp,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud with the reason.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין בּוֹדְקִין לֹא לְאוֹר הַחַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the verse-based source for lamplight, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that rules out other kinds of light.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בדיקת חמץ may not be done by sunlight, moonlight, or torchlight, only by the light of a lamp.
